item.content:encoded:
Plus 1'ed when I first read this as a main lister last night. Removed my vote at the Incident Log,1 because by that point it veered way to close to -j territory.

Came back to find its brand-spankin-new -j designation. (+1 yay!) Though I think this has potential for a mainliat spot. There's a lot of fridge horror with something so seemingly innocuous and silly crippling a shadow organization.

Was that final collapsible always there? Or is that a recent addition? 'Cause that's the point where I stop laughing and have an 'oh shit' moment…

Footnotes
1. Though it was pretty damn funny.

I'm considering reworking this as a -J, actually.

And to answer the question regarding perception, SCP-2618 will only appear as useful and necessary to everyone while standing on its own. When in the possession of an affected subject, everyone other than the subject will see it as a banana.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
So this reads pretty well and I like the idea… if it were a -J. As a matter of fact I'm astounded by the fact that you didn't make this a -J, because it sounds official enough and equally silly enough to be one. It even made ME laugh a bit and I don't normally laugh at anything. However, as a mainlist article I can't in good conscience upvote this due to the fact that it's absurdly short and not a very… fulfilling article, I guess. It's anomaly doesn't seem like it's enough to justify it being a scip rather than an anomalous item. I feel like maybe if there were more dialogue and scenarios in which it was used, it could be justifiable as a scip, but right now I'm not really sure why they wouldn't just… I don't know wall the trees off so no one could see the fruit. I'm gonna remain neutral for now.

Well my critique has been absolved so +1 :P
